appraisal_events.evidence: Saint-Loup me répondit que celle où allait Bloch devait être « extrêmement purée, le paradis du pauvre ».
appraisal_events.explanation: Saint-Loup dismisses the brothel Bloch frequents as cheap and low-status, implicitly disparaging Bloch's means and taste by contrast with the finer places he himself knows.

appraisal_events.evidence: cette vie scandaleuse, à celle de Charlus qui avait su... grandir encore sa situation de Guermantes... recherché, adulé par la société la plus choisie... avait ainsi été aussi bon mari que bon fils !
appraisal_events.explanation: Framed as Charlus's own hypothetical, self-serving justification for scolding Saint-Loup, this passage elevates his social standing and reputation as husband and son, but the narrator immediately follows with guarded skepticism about a secret he holds, casting doubt on the sincerity of the comparison.

status_effects.explanation: Mildly diminished by Saint-Loup's condescending characterization of his taste and means as inferior.
Locally elevated by a favorable, though ironically framed, comparison to Saint-Loup that stresses his enduring Guermantes prestige and role as good husband and son.

ambiguities: The candidate 'la mère du narrateur' does not actually appear in this passage: 'ma mère' occurs only in Saint-Loup's own speech ('je faisais de la peine à ma mère') and refers to Saint-Loup's mother, not the narrator's mother, so no event was attributed to this candidate.

Charlus's elevation (S2) is voiced as a hypothetical, self-serving perspective ('il eût parfaitement pu être sincère... du point de vue de l'homme du monde') rather than a flat narrator assertion, and is immediately followed by the narrator's guarded skepticism about a secret concerning Charlus's actual conduct, suggesting dramatic irony that this supplement scores conservatively.
